messages:
Jordan Lee: quick UX check: in the model catalog compare table the filter chips overflow on small widths and push the header actions off-canvas. i sketched 3 patterns: +N overflow (menu), horizontal scroll, and off-canvas drawer. which feels best for fast workflows?

Priya Singh: +N overflow. least disruptive and keeps the compare controls visible. just needs a clear affordance and announceable label for screen readers.

Devon Brooks: horizontal scroll looks nice but keyboard users lose context. drawer is fine but heavy for toggling. +N seems pragmatic if it's keyboard accessible.

Riley Park: agree +N. for mobile open it full-screen with checkboxes so you can multi-select; on desktop a small menu with checkboxes is fine. add a tooltip and aria-expanded on the button.

a11y-bot: accessibility pointers: add aria-label like "Show hidden filters (3)" on the overflow button; update aria-expanded on toggle; ensure menu has role=menu and items have role=menuitemcheckbox. announce a SR message when opened: "3 additional filters available". provide visible focus outlines (>=3:1).

Jordan Lee: noted. another thing: performance badges are low contrast in the current spec. a11y-bot flagged them.

Priya Singh: i'll propose updated tokens: darker teal for "fast", warmer amber for "cheap", and stronger gray for secondary badges. target 4.5:1 for badge text.

Devon Brooks: microcopy tweak: pinned label currently reads "Pinned v1.2.3" which runs together. suggest "Pinned  v1.2.3" using a mid-dot or bullet so it scans: "Pinned  v1.2.3". also add a hover tooltip that shows who pinned and when.

Riley Park: for keyboard behavior: ArrowDown should focus first menuitem, space/enter toggles checkbox, Escape closes and returns focus to overflow button. test with NVDA and VoiceOver.

Jordan Lee: decision: implement +N overflow menu for chip overflow (desktop) and full-screen multi-select on mobile, ensure proper ARIA roles and SR announcement, increase badge contrast to WCAG thresholds, and update pinned copy to use a mid-dot separator.

Jordan Lee: action items: @Riley prototype keyboard interactions and record a short demo (due Tue), @Priya update badge tokens + microcopy and open PR, @Devon create QA checklist for SR and keyboard flows, i'll add a unit/cypress keyboard test and update rollout notes.

Priya Singh: i'll attach color swatches and contrast ratios in the PR.

Devon Brooks: i'll run NVDA + VoiceOver passes and share any gaps.

Riley Park: will post the demo link when ready. :thumbsup:
